claims.text: The initial material is an equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy without nanoparticle reinforcement.
The intervention introduces approximately 2 vol% ultra-fine WC nanoparticles into CoCrFeMnNi.
The WC nanoparticles are introduced through in situ casting followed by rapid solidification.
The processing route will produce a uniform dispersion of WC nanoparticles in the HEA matrix.
Dispersed WC nanoparticles act as thermal bridges in the CoCrFeMnNi matrix.
Dispersed WC nanoparticles provide dispersion strengthening in the CoCrFeMnNi matrix.
WC has sufficiently high intrinsic thermal conductivity to improve heat transfer in the composite.
WC-mediated thermal bridging enhances electron and phonon heat transfer.
WC nanoparticles pin grain boundaries in the HEA.
Grain-boundary pinning inhibits grain coarsening during repeated thermal cycles.
Inhibition of grain coarsening maintains microstructural stability during repeated thermal cycles.
Adding approximately 2 vol% WC will increase effective thermal conductivity by about 15–20% relative to unreinforced CoCrFeMnNi.
Adding approximately 2 vol% WC will maintain or slightly improve yield strength relative to unreinforced CoCrFeMnNi.
The WC-modified alloy will retain structural stability under cyclic high-temperature loading.
The predicted improvements will hold at 700–900 °C under cyclic thermal-mechanical loading.
Inadequate WC dispersion could prevent the predicted benefits.
Unfavorable interfacial thermal resistance between WC and the HEA matrix could prevent the predicted thermal-conductivity benefit.
